speaker: Siddaramaiah
quote_english: Interest-free short-term loans will be made available to farmers up to Rs 2 lakh, and at 1 per cent interest for loans between Rs 2 lakh and Rs 3 lakh from cooperative institutions.
summary: The Karnataka government announced the interest-free crop loan scheme in July 2013 and reported disbursals to 10.5 lakh farmers by November 2013.

media.title: Karnataka government announces interest-free farm loan up to Rs 2 lakh
Farmers to get interest-free loans up to Rs 2 lakh, says Karnataka

evidence.title: State government to give out Rs 8,000 crore as farm loans, says Minister
evidence.key_figure: 10.5 lakh farmers covered and Rs 4,400 crore distributed; Rs 8,000 crore planned for 20 lakh farmers

evidence.title: K'taka to distribute grains at Re 1 per kg from October 2
evidence.key_figure: Small and marginal farmers to get interest-free loans up to Rs 2 lakh; 1 per cent for Rs 2-3 lakh

govt_response.title: Karnataka government confirms scheme rollout
govt_response.summary: The cooperation minister said 10.5 lakh farmers had been covered and Rs 4,400 crore distributed under the 2013-14 plan.

analysis: The scheme was announced in the revised 2013-14 budget and operationalised through cooperative institutions during the year. In August 2013 the government restated the terms: zero interest up to Rs 2 lakh and 1% for Rs 2-3 lakh. By November 2013 the cooperation minister reported 10.5 lakh farmers covered and Rs 4,400 crore disbursed, against a plan of Rs 8,000 crore for 20 lakh farmers. The announced policy was implemented, although disbursal was still in progress at that point.
notes: The quote is the reported budget announcement, not a transcript. The scheme was for short-term crop loans through cooperative institutions.
